First, I’ll parse the SVG path data:  

The path starts with `M 72.96,32.63 L 7.85,57.83` — that’s a move to (72.96,32.63) and a line to (7.85,57.83).  
Then `M 7.85,57.83 L 39.84,72.32` — move to the same point (7.85,57.83) and line to (39.84,72.32).  
Then `L 52.68,87.15` — line from last point to (52.68,87.15).  
Then `L 58.40,70.53` — line to (58.40,70.53).  
Then `L 81.67,51.69` — line to (81.67,51.69).  
Then `L 72.96,32.63` — line back to the start point (72.96,32.63).  

So the vertices in order are:  
1. (72.96,32.63)  
2. (7.85,57.83)  
3. (39.84,72.32)  
4. (52.68,87.15)  
5. (58.40,70.53)  
6. (81.67,51.69)  
7. back to (72.96,32.63)  

That’s 6 distinct vertices before closing:  
(72.96,32.63) → (7.85,57.83) → (39.84,72.32) → (52.68,87.15) → (58.40,70.53) → (81.67,51.69) → back to start.  

That’s 6 sides — a hexagon.  

Final answer: (C)
